alloy.preparation: Induction melted under argon, cast in air using the split-heat technique with successive Mo additions. Hot forged and hot rolled to 0.76 cm, then cold rolled to 0.38 cm; annealed at 1150 °C for 1 h and water quenched. Mounted in acrylic with one surface parallel to the rolling plane; polished by standard metallography to a distilled-water slurry of 0.3 µm alumina. Masked with Scotch 470 electroplater tape except for a 0.3 cm diameter circular area for pitting measurements.

test_solution.preparation: Argon saturated. The text discusses a change from pH 1 to 7 when comparing the media, but does not give an independently measured pH for each test; no numeric pH is assigned.

test_method.procedure_description: Masked electrode; saturated calomel reference and platinum auxiliary isolated by a glass frit. Potential scanned from −0.7 V in the active region into the passive region to form the passive film in situ. Usually 600 mV/hr until 0.2–0.3 V below expected pitting, then 60 mV/hr; scanning stopped within 20 mV after breakdown.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Sharp rise in passive current with microscopically confirmed pits; principal pitting potential is initiation followed by continued pit growth. Crevice-only runs were rejected.

experiments.result_note: Average of two or more runs. Table I analyzed Mo content is retained; nominal series compositions in Table III and captions may differ by rounding. Intermediate Table I analyses marked NA are not replaced with endpoint analyses; nominal Cr/Ni are identified as such here. Reported percent basis is not further specified. Material series: high.

test_solution.preparation: Argon saturated. The text discusses a change from pH 1 to 7 when comparing the media, but does not give an independently measured pH for each test; no numeric pH is assigned.

test_method.procedure_description: Masked electrode; saturated calomel reference and platinum auxiliary isolated by a glass frit. Potential scanned from −0.7 V in the active region into the passive region to form the passive film in situ. Usually 600 mV/hr until 0.2–0.3 V below expected pitting, then 60 mV/hr; scanning stopped within 20 mV after breakdown.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Sharp rise in passive current with microscopically confirmed pits; principal pitting potential is initiation followed by continued pit growth. Crevice-only runs were rejected.
